text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> INC98765: inference-prod-eu p99 latency > SLO threshold. Metric: p99_latency=1.85s (SLO=1.2s) · sustained 32m · paging oncall (priority: P1)

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Primary on-call (alex.p) notified. Runbook: /runbooks/latency-tail.json

Alex P: ack. I'm on the page, joining. Starting triage — which regions affected?

Maria G: I see the spike concentrated in eu-west-1, traffic routing shows a 40% increase there over the last 20m. p95 ~ 800ms, p99 ~ 1.8s. No large error increase though.

Jon K: +1 eu-west. Checking serving pool health now. Running quick checks:
```bash
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=infer -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.phase} {.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}
'{end}
```

Sam R: I'm seeing a KV cache miss rate jump in the telemetry (kv_cache_miss_rate from 2% -> 28%). Could be cache thrash after the 03:12 deploy. Anyone rolled a model or config?

Li W: Confirmed a small config tweak to batching was rolled 03:10 by ci/cd with canary flag - it should have been safe but might affect kernel selection under certain seq lengths. Rolling back to previous batching config now.

Alex P: Good call. Maria, can you check if requests are hitting fallback model variants (bigger models) due to cache misses? That would amplify latency.

Maria G: Looking at routing logs: ~12% of requests rerouted to model-large-fallback in eu-west over past 25m. That matches the latency profile.

Ash T: I'm scaling up the infer pool to absorb burst while rollback completes. Command: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment/infer-gpu --replicas=12`

Jon K: Also increasing auto-batcher capacity: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api.internal/v1/ops/autobatcher?scale=2` (doing graceful ramp).

incident-bot: Note added: rollback to batching-config v2 initiated by Li W at 1945679005.

Li W: rollback finished at 1945679030. Watching. Cache warm-up in progress (manual prefill kickstarted).

Sam R: After rollback, kv_cache_miss_rate trending down from 28% -> 6% over 4m. p95 improved to ~420ms. p99 still at 1.1s (better but above SLO).

Alex P: Great. We need to mitigate p99 tail further. Options: reduce default max_tokens for noisy routes, enable aggressive prefix caching for common prompts, or divert heavy customers to dedicated pool. Thoughts?

Maria G: Quick win: enable prefix/KV sticky cache for the top 20% of traffic patterns — I can flip the feature flag. It should cut backend token generation cost for repeated prompts.

Ash T: Flipped feature flag: `feature.kv_sticky_top20 = true`. Tested on canary — no errors.

pagerduty-bot: INC98765 acknowledged by Alex P at 1945679015.

Jon K: After sticky cache and scale, p95 now 350ms, p99 720ms. We're back under SLO for p99 in most regions, but eu-west shows a residual tail at 780-820ms on a small subset of requests.

Alex P: Okay, status: rollback + sticky cache + extra replicas = significant improvement. Keeping page open for 30m observation. If p99 stays < 1.2s for 30m we'll resolve.

Sam R: Noted a handful of long-running requests tied to routing to model-large-fallback for customers with long-context sessions. Proposing temporary routing policy: fallback->deprioritize to dedicated-eu pool and instead use small-model-degraded fallback to keep latency bounded.

Maria G: Implemented routing change: decreased fallback priority for model-large-fallback and enabled model-small-degraded as primary fallback at 1945679130.

Li W: Telemetry shows immediate drop in tail for affected sessions. p99 eu-west dropped to 630ms.

Alex P: Good. Start communication: updating incident status page and notifying support to flag any customers with higher SLAs. Sam, can you draft a short blurb for support with root cause and mitigation?

Sam R: Drafting now: "We observed a KV cache thrash after a batching config change which increased cache misses and caused elevated p99 latency in eu-west. We rolled back the config, scaled inference pool, and enabled sticky caching and adjusted fallback routing, which brought p99 back under SLO. We're monitoring; no customer error impact observed."

Ash T: We should schedule a postmortem to review deploy validation for batching config. Also adding a short-term alert: kv_cache_miss_rate >= 10% -> notify infra team before paging oncall.

Alex P: Agreed. I'll set the postmortem and assign owner. For now, monitoring for 30m. If no regression, we'll resolve and close INC98765.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: INC98765 status updated -> Monitoring period active (30m) by Alex P.

Maria G: One minor note: a handful of low-volume customers in APAC routed through eu-west had slightly increased latency ~200ms extra — support blurb includes that. No errors.

Jon K: Logging snapshot captured for later RCA. Command used: `kubectl -n prod logs -l app=infer --since=40m > /tmp/incident_IN98765_logs.txt`

Alex P: Thanks team. I'll close the page if stable. Keeping this thread for final notes and postmortem link.

(30m later)

Alex P: p99 steady at 600ms eu-west, p95 320ms. No regen in alerts. Resolving INC98765.

pagerduty-bot: INC98765 marked resolved by Alex P at 1945679280.

Alex P: Closing notes: probable cause = batching config change caused higher KV cache churn leading to fallback to larger models. Mitigations: rollback, scale, sticky cache flag, fallback routing change. Action items: 1) postmortem owner: Alex P; 2) add pre-deploy KV churn test to canary job (owner: Li W); 3) add pre-alert for kv_cache_miss_rate (owner: Sam R).

Maria G: Thanks all. Good catch and quick rollback.

Sam R: +1, will open the postmortem ticket.

incident-bot: Note: postmortem ticket PMT-214 opened by Sam R.
